picks.title: How to tell if your sourdough is proofed
picks.reason: Explains the poke test for final proof: a quick bounce-back means it needs more time, a slow return with a slight dent means it's ready, and a dent that stays means over-proofed. This is the readiness check you need after the fridge proof.

evidence.quote: If you poke it and it bounces back quickly, it needs more time.
If you poke it and it leaves a dent, or your dough starts to deflate, it has over proofed.
If you poke it and it comes back nice a slowly leaving only a slight indentation, it's ready to bake.

picks.confidence_note: The quotes spell out the criteria. It is a 2-minute explainer that doesn't cover fridge timing.

warnings: None of the 36 candidates has a transcript. Every pick rests on chapter lists and descriptions, so teaching quality is unverified and confidence is moderate at best.
Total viewing time is about 92 minutes, roughly 77% of the 120 budget. I did not pad the rest with weaker or redundant videos.

The plan has three recipes: Brian Lagerstrom, Keep it Sweet Kitchen and The Bread Code. Use the Keep it Sweet Kitchen bake-along as the single recipe to bake from. Use the others for concepts and cues, because their hydration and timings differ.
Brian Lagerstrom's levain ferments for about 12 hours at room temperature. If you want that levain method, plan to build it the night before mixing.
I assumed you have a Dutch oven or a similar lidded pot, and that a cold retard of overnight or longer is wanted.

No good source was found for a dedicated explanation of baker's percentages. Hydration is covered only inside the pick videos, so check the recipe weights in the bake-along against the one video that states them.
